page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m2.large is a burstable, entry-level virtual server instance belonging to the shared-core t6 family. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration exposes 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX-512 vector extensions with VNNI support, AES cryptography, and FMA instructions. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it has a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate compute and memory output consistent with a lower-tier burstable profile. The instance achieved 1300.19 on the single-core stress-ng CPU test and 2402.69 under multi-core stress testing, both positioning in the lower 25 percent tier. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 1045.0 and a multi-core score of 1850.0. Memory bandwidth reached 186.46 GB/sec for small cached reads, falling to 20.68 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 16.39 GB/sec for uncached writes. Under Passmark testing, the instance posted an overall CPU score of 2464.26 and a memory score of 1088.85.

The qualitative cost structure of this instance favors low-utilization scenarios where continuous computational power is unnecessary. Because CPU time is shared and burstable, sustained intensive compute is constrained by CPU credit limits and lower multi-core scaling. The lack of onboard storage requires relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistent data. This profile is structurally matched to non-critical development environments, small background automation tasks, low-traffic internal web portals, and microservices with sporadic request patterns.
